result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both give a direct yes with the location, then go well past the brief answer the rubric asks for. A has the rep ask three scripted questions, tell them to 'stop talking', and add pre-call checks. B offers one light question or a quick live demo depending on the buyer, so it is closer to the ideal, even though its branches and tips still make it long. Neither invents features: both mention scheduled exports or integrations only as things the product may not have. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers open with a clear yes and the one-click, top-right location. A then adds conditional branches and tips, but its main advice stays 'say what it does and stop', with at most one optional question. B turns the yes into a three-part discovery question and adds pre-call checks and pipeline-stage advice, which is too much for a simple yes. Both are longer than a few lines, and both mention scheduled exports or integrations only with caveats, not as claimed features.
